shared_elements: low-relief figures carved on a flat vertical stone surface
bird head shown in profile with prominent beak
wing rendered with rows of feathers
repeated small motifs filling background/border areas
justification: The clearest correspondence is that both surfaces carry profile bird-headed forms with feathered wings and both use a horizontal division across the field, but in A these are freestanding schematic animals (quadrupeds, birds, snake-like forms) stacked in registers, while B shows a single large anthropomorphic winged figure with human body, raised arm, and handled bucket framed by rosette borders. The manner of depiction differs utterly: A is minimal, flattened and schematic with plain unmodelled bodies, whereas B is densely detailed and anatomically modelled with patterned garment, musculature and hair.
